chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Muhammad ibn Shurayh who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the going out of the women during the two Eids, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'No, except for the elderly woman wearing their pair of shoes'.

key_terms.الْعِيدَيْنِ: The two Eids (Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha)
key_terms.مَنْقَلَاهَا: Her manqalah (a specific type of footwear or covering for shoes)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on women going out for Eid prayers in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the general permissibility of women attending Eid prayers by addressing the specific concern of ritual purity during travel. He permits elderly women to wear their 'manqalah' (often interpreted as thick shoes or coverings for the feet) to facilitate walking on potentially impure ground, thereby avoiding the need for frequent *khuf* wiping or changing footwear. This ruling highlights the practical accommodations made in Shia jurisprudence for women's participation in communal worship while maintaining ritual cleanliness.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Marwan Bin Muslim, from Muhammad Bin Shurayh who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the going out of the women during the two Eids, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, except for the elderly woman wearing their pair of shoes’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from Marwan ibn Muslim from Muhammad ibn Shurayh who has said the following: “This is concerning my question before abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about women’s going out for the two ‘Id.
He (the Imam) said, ‘No, except old women wearing their pairs of shoes.’” (Consult Fatwah about this hadith)
